_readme: Surface templates for the Sindhi reasoning corpus. This file is intended to be edited
by hand: it is the place where human-authored templates live alongside the
generated ones. Run `python -m common.reasoning.check_templates --language sindhi`
after editing: it validates the schema, checks every literal word against the Sindhi
pretraining corpus, and prints a rendered example of each template.
Each template has two parts. `fact` is emitted once per entity (value_compare) or
once per adjacent pair (chain); `question` is emitted once at the end. Splitting
them this way is what lets one template cover 2, 3 or 4 entities, which is how the
held-out longer-chain test split is built without writing separate templates for it.
Placeholders need not be written by hand. A sentence written with real
words and convert it:  python -m common.reasoning.make_template --language sindhi
--fact "<one statement>" --question "<the question>" --type argmax
prints a finished template to paste here, and names any word it did not
recognise. The placeholder list below is reference, not a prerequisite.
PLACEHOLDERS
{e0} {e1} {e2} ...  entity name by position
{ea} {eb}           the two entities of one chain link (inside `fact` only)
{e}  {v}            entity and its value (inside a value_compare `fact` only)
{efirst} {elast}    first and last entity of a chain (inside `question` only)
{attr} {poss}       attribute noun and its possessive  (عمر, جي)
{noun_gender}       not a placeholder - selects {who_poss} automatically
{unit} {cop}        unit and copula                    (سال, آهي)
{than}              comparison particle                (کان)
{more} {less}       invariant quantifiers              (وڌيڪ, گهٽ)
{sup_more} {sup_less}  superlatives                    (سڀ کان وڌيڪ, سڀ کان گهٽ)
{who} {who_poss}    interrogatives                     (ڪير, ڪنهن جي/ڪنهن جو)
{or} {equal}        disjunction and equality           (يا, برابر)
{fs} {qm}           full stop and question mark        (., ؟)
fact_reverse        chain only - the same link stated from the opposite end, so the larger entity is not always named first
FIELDS
id             unique, stable - referenced in the results tables
family         value_compare | chain
question_type  argmax | argmin | relation
split          train | heldout   (heldout templates build test_template)
author         generated | user  (provenance, reported honestly in the writeup)
A NOTE ON WHAT MAKES A GOOD TEMPLATE: vary the word order and register, not the
vocabulary. The vocabulary is already corpus-validated; new words would have to go
through candidates.py instead. Templates that only swap synonyms add little, while
templates that reorder the clause genuinely test whether the model learned the
relation or a fixed word sequence.

templates.question: {attr} {sup_more} {who_poss} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: generated
templates.notes: word order variant: attribute fronted before the superlative

templates.question: {entities} مان {who_poss} {attr} {more} {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: mirror of H-VC-argmax-user2. Sindhi says this with the single word `مان` (97,000) where Hindi needs two (`में से`).

templates.question: {who} {more} {attr} جو {cop}{qm}
templates.author: user
templates.notes: mirror of H-VC-argmax-user4, with `جو` literal for the same reason.
